stories.title: AIIMS performs India's first open fetal surgery for spina bifida
stories.summary: Doctors at AIIMS Delhi have performed the country's first open fetal surgery to repair a lumbosacral myelomeningocele in a 25-week-old fetus. The six-hour procedure followed five weeks of multidisciplinary planning and simulation. Both the mother and the fetus are currently reported to be stable and recovering well.

stories.title: Single amino acid change improves influenza B vaccine
stories.summary: Researchers in Beijing report that a single amino acid substitution in the hemagglutinin protein of an influenza B vaccine candidate broadens its protective capacity in mice. The modification restores a glycosylation motif, addressing a limitation in current seasonal vaccines. The findings were published in Frontiers in Microbiology.

stories.title: CRISPR treatment lowers blood fats in monkeys for three years
stories.summary: A single infusion of a gene-editing treatment successfully lowered triglyceride levels in monkeys for three years. The experiment suggests that gene-editing technologies could provide a lasting alternative to traditional lipid-lowering medications for those at risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. The long-term effects were observed in a controlled study.

stories.title: Scientists map cellular atlas of the basal ganglia
stories.summary: Researchers have created a cellular atlas of the basal ganglia, a brain region linked to movement, habit formation, and decision-making. The map includes data from humans, mice, and monkeys. The team suggests this work could guide future treatments for conditions including Parkinson’s disease, bipolar disorder, and addiction.

stories.title: Telangana government to support new public health university
stories.summary: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy has pledged state support for the Public Health Foundation of India to establish its Institute of Public Health Sciences in Hyderabad. The government has set a June 2, 2028, deadline for the campus, promising assistance with land, funding, and necessary regulatory permissions.

stories.title: PM Modi credits Ayushman Bharat with significant medical savings
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated that the Ayushman Bharat programme has saved families 2.25 lakh crore rupees in medical costs. The Prime Minister described the scheme as a priority for the government, noting that it provides health insurance protection to more than 60 per cent of Indian families.

Ayushman Bharat may restrict 112 treatments to government hospitals
stories.summary: State health authorities are reviewing a proposal to reserve 112 specialised medical treatments exclusively for public facilities under the Ayushman Bharat scheme starting December 1. The change could shift patient traffic away from private empanelled networks, potentially limiting access for beneficiaries currently using those private facilities.

stories.title: Ayushman Bharat shifts 112 treatments to public hospitals
stories.summary: Beneficiaries of the Ayushman Bharat scheme must visit government hospitals for 112 medical procedures starting December 1, 2026. The National Health Authority is moving these packages from private facilities to public centres, adding to the 23 procedures already restricted. The shift aims to standardise care nationwide.

stories.title: India reports 38 percent drop in TB mortality
stories.summary: India recorded a 38 percent reduction in TB mortality since 2015, with rates falling from 28 to 18 per lakh population by 2025. The Union Health Ministry reported a 94 percent treatment success rate for drug-susceptible cases, aligning with findings from the World Health Organization Global Tuberculosis Report 2026.

stories.title: Health ministry considers appeal on intern stipend parity
stories.summary: The Union Health Ministry is considering an appeal against the National Medical Commission regarding stipend parity for undergraduate medical interns. Despite two letters from the ministry, the commission has yet to act. Interns often work shifts exceeding 30 hours. The commission previously acknowledged the existence of pay differences.

stories.title: Medical interns stipend parity: Union Health ministry considers appeal against NMC
stories.summary: NEW DELHI: The Union Health Ministry is considering an appeal against the National Medical Commission’s (NMC) inaction on stipend parity for all undergraduate medical interns, whether in government or private colleges, according to an RTI. This follows the ministry’s two letters to the NMC, asking it to examine stipend parity.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu halts public health bulletins
stories.summary: The Tamil Nadu Directorate of Public Health and Preventive Medicine has stopped publishing its monthly bulletins and medical journal. Officials stated the move prevents the misrepresentation of data by the media. Public health experts have raised concerns regarding the resulting lack of transparency in reporting disease and mortality rates.

stories.title: India TB mortality falls faster than global average
stories.summary: India achieved a 38 percent reduction in TB mortality since 2015, outpacing the global average of 35 percent. According to the World Health Organization, the country also reached a 94 percent treatment success rate for drug-susceptible TB. India accounts for approximately one quarter of all new global cases.

stories.title: US measles elimination status expected to be revoked
stories.summary: Plummeting vaccination rates have triggered a wave of measles, with the Pan American Health Organization expected to revoke the US elimination status held since 2000. Experts report the country is facing its worst outbreak since 1991, ending a 26-year streak of limited local transmission.

stories.title: US loses measles elimination status
stories.summary: The United States has officially lost its status as a country where measles is eliminated, according to global health authorities. The Pan American Health Organization concluded that the virus has reestablished regular transmission. Elimination status requires sporadic outbreaks to end within one year, a benchmark no longer being met.

stories.title: WHO activates highest emergency response for El Niño
stories.summary: The World Health Organization has activated a Grade 3 emergency response to El Niño-related health risks. India is identified as a high-risk country facing potential heatwaves, dengue, malaria, and food insecurity. The organisation warns that changing weather patterns threaten to disrupt healthcare services and increase infectious disease transmission.

stories.title: Gaza health ministry reports attacks on all 36 hospitals
stories.summary: Gaza’s Ministry of Health announced that all 36 hospitals in the territory have been attacked since the start of the war. The ministry claims 176 healthcare facilities have been targeted, resulting in nearly 1,000 deaths among medical personnel and civilians. Many facilities are now completely out of service.

stories.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) continues to spread amid repeated and ongoing deadly attacks on civilians and frontline health workers by armed groups that are obstructing efforts to stop transmission, UN responders said on Friday. Israeli strike hits Nasser Hospital in Gaza
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike hit the surgical wing of Nasser Hospital in southern Gaza, killing six people including a surgeon and a 13-year-old boy. The Israeli military stated it targeted a Hamas commander, though the individual was not among the dead. No evidence was provided for the military claim.

stories.title: Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills 6, Health Ministry says

stories.title: Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills 6, including surgeon and child, Health Ministry says
stories.summary: An Israeli strike hit Nasser Hospital in southern Gaza early Thursday, killing six people, including a surgeon and a 13-year-old boy, Gaza’s Health Ministry said. At least 28 people were wounded. The Israeli military said it targeted a Hamas commander and other militants at the hospital but provided no evidence.

stories.title: Healthcare organizations struggle to document AI model checks
stories.summary: CHIME's 2026 report found that 93.2 percent of surveyed healthcare organizations use AI, with full generative AI adoption reaching 54.8 percent. However, only 16.4 percent of these users fully document model monitoring after deployment. Governance remains a task for the future.

stories.title: EkaCare to provide AI voice scribes for Indian public health
stories.summary: The National Health Authority has selected EkaCare as a technology partner for its ambient AI-enabled voice scribe solution. The tool is designed to convert doctor-patient conversations into structured clinical documentation for public health organizations under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission. It runs on NHA infrastructure.

stories.title: Zus Health raises $33 million for clinical data infrastructure
stories.summary: Zus Health secured $33 million in series B funding to build a connected patient data layer for AI-powered clinical workflows. The round, led by Drive Capital, brings the company's total capital raised to over $100 million. The startup aims to provide the foundation for reliable healthcare AI.

stories.title: India expands AI use in national healthcare delivery
stories.summary: India is integrating AI tools across its healthcare system to improve disease detection and remote care. Government data indicates that AI-enabled tools in the National TB Elimination Programme have contributed to a 27 percent decline in adverse tuberculosis outcomes. The government cites gains in service quality and affordability.

stories.title: Happiest Health commits 500 crore to digital health expansion
stories.summary: Happiest Health plans to invest 500 crore in technology over five years, with half allocated to its new digital health business. The company intends to roll out 11 applications within 18 months, including a diabetes management tool that combines AI assistance with continuous glucose monitoring.

stories.title: Study finds mental health challenges in children with diabetes
stories.summary: A PGI study of 97 children with Type 1 Diabetes found that 20 percent exceeded thresholds for significant psychological maladjustment. While average mental health scores matched local norms, depression showed a link to long-term blood sugar averages. The findings were published in the Journal of Pediatric Endocrinology and Metabolism.

stories.title: Insomnia linked to increased risk of major health conditions
stories.summary: A study published in Sleep Medicine Reviews analyzed millions of participants and found insomnia linked to a 26 percent increased risk of stroke. The research also associated sleep issues with higher risks of dementia and mental health conditions. The findings do not establish a direct causal link.

stories.title: Choir participation may benefit children with heart conditions
stories.summary: A study from Lurie Children's Hospital found that choir singing may improve lung function and decrease anxiety in children born with a single heart ventricle. The intervention included singing and breathing instruction. Researchers noted improvements in perceived school functioning for participants.

stories.title: Higher Grocery Prices Linked with Worse Food Insufficiency, Mental Health - GantNews.com
Psychiatric assessments often show disagreement between youth and caregivers
stories.summary: A study published in JAMA Psychiatry found that youth and their caregivers frequently disagree on psychiatric diagnoses. Researchers at UC San Diego concluded that relying on a single informant can influence which mental health problems are identified. Disagreement is described as the typical norm.

stories.title: Sports club participation linked to teen well-being
stories.summary: A study of 162 middle school students in Austria found that participation in sports clubs is significantly linked to improved psychosocial well-being. The research suggests that regular physical activity may be more strongly associated with perceived well-being than cardiorespiratory fitness levels alone.

stories.title: Urban renewal linked to improved mental health in older adults
stories.summary: A longitudinal analysis of older adults in China suggests that coordinated urban renewal initiatives substantially enhance late-life mental health and alleviate depressive symptoms. The study examined how physical and infrastructural improvements across domestic and municipal environments influence psychological wellbeing. The environment is now considered a medical intervention.

stories.title: KIMS rheumatologist presents telemedicine research in Seoul
stories.summary: Prof. Sakir Ahmed of KIMS presented research on telerheumatology and AI usage at the Asia Pacific League against Rheumatology annual meeting in Seoul. The presentation highlighted work conducted by his team across the Asia-Pacific region and India. Telemedicine continues to find new venues for discussion.

stories.title: Mental health conditions common in Prader-Willi syndrome
stories.summary: An Australian study found that nearly three-quarters of people with Prader-Willi syndrome have a diagnosed or parent-reported mental health condition, with anxiety being the most prevalent. Nearly half of children younger than 12 also reported concerns, many without a formal diagnosis. Early screening remains a primary recommendation.

stories.title: Mental health first aid guidelines adapted for Namibia
stories.summary: A Delphi consensus study published in BMC Psychiatry has adapted Mental Health First Aid guidelines for suicide prevention in Namibia. Researchers worked with local professionals and people with lived experience to tailor evidence-based recommendations to local cultural contexts. Guidelines are now being adjusted for local application.

stories.title: Mental health diagnoses rise among active duty soldiers
stories.summary: More than 560,000 active-duty United States service members were diagnosed with at least one mental health disorder between 2020 and 2024. While annual incidence rates rose through 2022, anxiety diagnoses continued to climb through 2024. The military is tracking the trend.

stories.title: Study analyzes youth mental health disclosures on social media
stories.summary: Researchers analyzed 957 posts and 763 comments on Reddit and TikTok to investigate how young people disclose mental health challenges online. The study evaluated user motivations and peer responses to disclosures of anxiety and depression. Social media is increasingly serving as a public diagnostic space.

research.title: Exercise after ACL surgery may protect knees from early osteoarthritis
research.summary: A new study suggests that the right kind of exercise could help protect young adults from early knee osteoarthritis following ACL surgery. Researchers found that a four-month supervised rehabilitation program improved pain, muscle strength, and quality of life without damaging knee cartilage. The findings challenge fears that exercise.

research.title: Stanford scientists discover hidden brain signals that predict Alzheimer’s years before symptoms
research.summary: Stanford researchers have discovered that hidden patterns of brain activity can predict Alzheimer’s risk years before memory problems appear, potentially offering an earlier warning than traditional biomarkers. The same patterns also reveal which brains are unusually resistant to aging, raising hopes for future treatments that could help protect.

research.title: Yale scientists reveal what really slows aging and what doesn't
research.summary: Yale researchers have discovered that certain prescription drugs, healthy diets, and exercise can measurably slow biological aging, while popular anti-aging supplements appear largely ineffective. Their analysis of 51 studies could transform how scientists evaluate anti-aging treatments, although whether these biological changes actually extend life remains uncertain.
